spec.title: PROP-019: Organization consumer licensing and distribution evidence

status.comment: organization/source/artifact release mechanisms pass full native floor; actual commercial approvals remain campaign inputs

p.ORGANIZATION-POLICY-FORMAT: codkitOrganizationPolicy:1 declares organization profile ID/revision, own holders and license expression, approved/forbidden third-party expressions, approved exceptions, a LicenseRef namespace, exact canonical custom-license texts with SHA-256, distribution notice/SBOM/carrier requirements and optional legal-review reference and optional trusted standardLicenseTexts for standard license/approved-exception notice text. Standard text records require installed SPDX IDs or approved exception IDs, unique identities, nonempty LF-only text with final LF and exact SHA-256; profiles omitting this field retain their previous parsed bytes. The schema is strict and types derive from it. SPDX identifiers come from the installed list. NOASSERTION, undeclared/foreign-namespace LicenseRef and missing/changed text/hash refuse. Custom texts are LF-only with a final LF and no BOM. This profile applies to consumer scope and never weakens Codkit's separate installed supply policy.

p.ORGANIZATION-POLICY-TRUST: A user/admin composition root supplies the policy directory; the default is the user .codkit directory. organization-policies.json carries strict codkitOrganizationPolicyStore:1 with v1 records or explicit store v2 with validated v1/v2 records. Store reads use contained regular-file I/O, validate every profile and refuse conflicting IDs including case aliases. A directory inside the physical patchset or an alias resolving into it refuses. No cwd/patchset fallback or patchset-supplied policy path is accepted. The selected policy and raw store bytes each receive their own digest; a digest is not an invented signature or legal approval.

p.ORGANIZATION-POLICY-SELECTION: Patchset selection contains only profile ID and optional additionalForbidden expressions. Holders, allowlists, license text, policy locations and other authority fields refuse. Additional prohibitions are monotone and cannot enable a license. Own scope uses the exact declared own expression in v1, or the path-selected trusted expression in v2; third-party scope uses exact approved expression combinations and forbidden identifiers/expressions. AND/OR/WITH and bounded parentheses are syntax, never automatic inference of legal permissions; an OR combination not explicitly approved remains refused.

p.CONSUMER-LICENSE-CHECK: Consumer source scanning uses the same sidecar/override/header/annotation precedence and nested REUSE matching as supply scanning, but its readers prove contained regular-file paths and its permission verdicts come only from the selected organization policy. All stated copyright holders must be organization holders for own scope; mixed/foreign holders remain third-party, with provenance annotation required. Modifications copyright does not replace upstream ownership. Exactly one SPDX expression and own copyright year are required; orphan sidecars and source symlinks refuse. Carrier/annotation license and foreign-holder disagreement refuse; third-party provenance requires a nonempty origin comment and binds the actual REUSE registry path/bytes/copyright/comment. Own sidecars/override annotations cannot erase declared upstream ownership in the original header. Checked source bytes, exact carrier path/bytes and selected policy digest bind a deterministic codkitConsumerLicenseCheck:1 report. Existing Codkit supply rules and default carrier readers remain unchanged; consumer-specific permissions never alter the supply authority. The header `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS` lays out in either style resolves to an own carrier of the policy holder: the copyright line carries the year and the holder and nothing after them (decision of 2026-11-01; a unit test runs the two against each other, `HEADER-FROM-PROFILE`).

p.CONSUMER-LICENSE-CLI: `codkit license consumer-check <dir> --profile <id>` inspects the explicit source directory read-only. A resolved patchset root is required solely to enforce the trusted-store boundary; neither fork nor codkit.json nor adapter execution is needed. The operator selects only a profile ID; the policy store is the fixed user ~/.codkit/organization-policies.json, without cwd/patchset fallback or a policy-directory flag. JSON data is the versioned consumer report, codes are 0 complete, 1 incomplete source evidence and 2 invalid invocation or unavailable trusted profile. The existing supply `license check` remains separate and unchanged.

p.DISTRIBUTION-NOTICE-CHECK: Notice attachment inspection captures the actual declared distribution inventory before and after reads. Each directory output carries every policy-required notice at its root; file outputs carry notices as separately declared sibling output files. A complete Git publish delivery is one bundle: its required notice is at the delivery root and still must be among actual tracked outputs; publication does not require redundant notices in every source subdirectory. This grouping comes from trusted operation composition, never an untrusted exemption. A notice existing only in source, in another bundle or below the bundle root does not satisfy attachment. Notice-only or empty output sets refuse. Notice bytes must be nonempty UTF-8, contained regular files; exact notice bytes, paths, selected policy and artifact inventory digests bind codkitDistributionNotices:1. Changed output snapshots or notice bytes refuse, and report status follows actual problems. This receipt proves named attachment and observed bytes only; approval of notice content, provenance, source carriers and SBOM remain separate distribution requirements, never inferred legal approval.

p.DISTRIBUTION-PROVENANCE: codkitDistributionDeclaration:1 maps each delivered payload file/link to inspected source paths and an explicit license expression. Every actual payload is covered exactly once; missing, duplicate, extra or uninspected paths refuse. Only trusted composition can approve regular-file metadata exclusions after their notice/SBOM checks; declaration alone cannot hide a payload. Fresh consumer inspection must be complete and nonempty. Foreign holders and origin-registry evidence stay in third-party scope. Complete source expressions, including AND/OR/WITH, are preserved; multiple distinct expressions require their deterministic parenthesized AND combination to be explicitly approved by v1 or third-party policy; v2 all-own artifacts retain the exact AND of individually scope-approved source expressions, never an inferred permission or rewritten upstream obligation. Actual source/carrier/registry bytes, authority/store/additional prohibitions, declaration and payload hashes bind codkitDistributionProvenance:1. Before/after source and artifact inspections refuse moved snapshots. The build mapping remains a declaration, not a cryptographic proof of compilation or an external legal approval.

p.DISTRIBUTION-DOCUMENTS: The deterministic version-1 NOTICE content and selected SPDX-2.3 JSON export derive from policy-checked payload provenance, not from absent minified headers. Notice includes component, selected authority, inspected sources/carriers/origin and exact trusted texts for every used standard/custom license and exception. A standard SPDX identifier alone never substitutes for its required notice text; missing or mismatched trusted text refuses. SPDX binds every declared payload path and SHA-256, explicit license conclusion, source mapping and exact extracted LicenseRef text; file-level copyright and in-file license information are not invented from source. Metadata files are excluded from document-content digests to avoid self-reference; adding finalized NOTICE/SBOM leaves expected documents unchanged while final inventory receipts still bind their bytes. SPDX creation time is an explicit whole-second UTC timestamp; namespace changes with document content. Moved authority, invalid identities/time and tampered custom text refuse. Attached documents must match expected UTF-8 bytes exactly and actual payload receipts still match. No general SPDX importer or eternal SBOM choice is promised; the strict owned export subset is versioned by external SPDX-2.3 and validated against that version.

p.RELEASE-LICENSING-SELECTION: The fixed patchset codkit.licensing.json carries codkitReleaseLicensing:1, profile ID/additional prohibitions, component identity, explicit UTC creation time, contained source directory and separate package/publish payload declarations with SBOM attachment path. It contains no policy path, holders, allowlist or trusted-text authority. Absent declaration preserves legacy release behavior with missing organization evidence explicit; a present declaration requires its requested operation and successful gates, not a fallback. Trusted user/admin composition selects the external store. Metadata exclusions are exactly policy-required attached notices and selected SBOM. Canonical documents and actual payload/provenance must agree; required delivered carriers are inspected only within actual outputs, with licensing metadata parsed or canonical-text matched. Package checks precede restoration, then final output and declaration/store receipts are rechecked. Publish reads the immutable selected Git blob, rejects changed snapshot bytes and retains the original patchset store boundary; a temporary checkout of the shaped tip, with hydrated LFS when needed, is inspected before real delivery. Component declaration/flag disagreement refuses. Receipt binds selected organization authority and distribution requirements without claiming a signature, commercial ruling or compiler proof. Mechanism acceptance is backed by the complete native suite; actual external organization/legal/signing/partner approvals are separate campaign inputs, not fixture claims.

p.ORGANIZATION-DISTRIBUTION-EVIDENCE: Consumer source scanning, actual artifact NOTICE/carrier checks and selected SBOM export must bind the selected trusted policy before package/publish enforcement is accepted. A minified artifact without required attached notice is incomplete/red even when source headers were valid. Report evidence complete/incomplete, never a legal-compatibility ruling. Mechanism fixtures are labelled examples, not real commercial approvals or external partner evidence.

p.ORGANIZATION-OWN-SCOPES: Policy/store v1 retain their strict shape and original bytes; v1 never admits own scope fields or v2 profiles. Explicit organization policy v2 keeps a default ownLicense and adds ownLicenseScopes with contained repository-relative glob paths and exact licence expressions; store v2 holds validated v1/v2 profiles. All scopes come from user/admin authority, not patchset selection. A source must provide its contained path; one matching scope overrides the default, zero matches uses the default, and multiple matching scopes refuse even when their expressions coincide. Unsafe/repeated patterns and unapproved standard/custom licence identifiers refuse. Scope resolution cannot change ownership, erase foreign provenance, rewrite upstream licensing or weaken additional prohibitions. An all-own assembled artifact keeps the exact AND of inspected, independently policy-checked source expressions; OR/partial substitution refuses. Source-to-artifact/carrier/policy hashes and original report/SPDX formats remain intact. Custom licence text and third-party approvals must come from actual authority, never invented to turn a fixture or consumer green. Versioned scopes do not assert legal compatibility of derivative distribution.

consumer-surfaces.title: Consumer surfaces: the profile carried into own files, manifests and the distributable (2026-11-01)

p.LICENSING-DECLARATION-V2: `codkit.licensing.json` version 2 keeps every field of version 1 (`profile`, `additionalForbidden`, `componentId`, `created`, `sourceDirectory`, the optional `package` and `publish` operations) and adds an optional `product` block of display choices: `licenseFile` (the base name of the product's licence file, default `LICENSE.md`), `title` (the human name of the licence used in headers), `holder` (one of the policy's `holders`, default the first), `year` (four digits, default the year of the run), `url` (a licence URL; absent, the family's URL fields are removed) and `retiredNotices` (phrases that must not survive in own files or licence surfaces; the guard forbids them). A `holder` outside the policy, a `title` or `licenseFile` that is empty or carries a path separator, a `year` that is not four digits refuse with `CK-E-CONFIG`. Version 1 reads exactly as before; nothing in either version can name a licence, a text or a permission - those stay with the trusted store (`ORGANIZATION-POLICY-TRUST`). Reading the declaration without an operation (`gen`, `verify`, `license annotate --own`) requires only `profile` and the store; `package` and `publish` keep requiring their operation block.

p.HEADER-FROM-PROFILE: When the patch set carries `codkit.licensing.json`, `gen feature`, `gen brand` and `gen licensing` lay the header of every generated file out from the selected profile: the holder of the `product` block (else the policy's first holder), the own expression resolved for the generated file's path (`ORGANIZATION-OWN-SCOPES`), the year of the `product` block (else the year of the run), the title and the licence file of the `product` block, in the style the type's `licensing.headerStyle` names (`line` when the type answers no area). `--holder`, `--license`, `--year` and `--header-style` still take effect and must agree with the profile: a holder outside `holders` or an expression other than the resolved own one is `CK-E-CONFIG` with nothing written. `--header-file` keeps the house form, and its text must resolve to a carrier (`CONSUMER-LICENSE-CHECK`) naming a policy holder and the own expression, else `CK-E-CONFIG`. A generated file never leaves the run without a header while a profile is selected. Without a declaration the behaviour of `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS` is unchanged.

p.GEN-LICENSING: `codkit gen licensing` writes the licence surfaces of the product from the profile and the type's `licensing` area, into the patch set, needing the fork tree for the pin's bytes: (1) for every `field` an overlay operation on its target - `expression` sets the own expression resolved for the target's scope, `file-name` sets `product.licenseFile`, `url` sets `product.url` or removes the key - merged into the existing overlay of that target when one exists (an operation with the same path is replaced, the others are kept, the document stays canonical) or written as a new overlay with the next free id, `expectUpstream` read from the target at the pin; (2) an add-file patch for `<licenceFileDirectory>/<licenseFile>` whose body is the canonical text of the own expression - the policy's custom text, or its trusted standard text; an own expression with no text in the policy refuses; (3) an add-file patch `<componentLicenceDirectory>/LICENSE-<component>.txt` for every `upstreamLicenceFile`, byte for byte from the pin, and `LICENSE-codkit.txt` with the tool's own licence text when the runtime library is delivered into the own layer (`delta/own/codkit/` exists); (4) every `rendering` from the canonical text - `rtf` as a plain RTF document (one paragraph per line, the headings of a Markdown source bold, every character outside ASCII as a `\u` escape), `text` with the Markdown marks stripped; (5) the guard (`LICENCE-GUARD`). Ids are the next free numbers in `licensing.subsystem`; the owner is the only one of `owners.json` or `--owner`; the patches are `extend`/`follow` with the guard's suite among their contract tests; the pin is the configuration's. The command refuses existing targets like every `gen` (`CK-E-GEN-EXISTS`, nothing written); `--update` rewrites exactly the artifacts of this command - a new edition of the text takes this path; `--dry-run` prints the plan. A type without the area is `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY`; no declaration is `CK-E-CONFIG`. The run ends with the reminders: declare the unit of the guard, run `license annotate --own`, run `verify`.

p.ANNOTATE-OWN: `codkit license annotate --own [--replace-retired] [--dry-run] [<paths…>]` gives the own files of the patch set their carriers from the profile: it walks `delta/own/**` and `delta/own-extensions/**` (the given paths narrow the walk), skips the tool's delivered paths (`delta/own/codkit/**`), the own manifest and existing sidecars, and never walks `delta/resources/**` - a resource that replaces an upstream file is a derivative work until a person says otherwise, so it is annotated by path when it is the product's own work. A file with a comment style receives the family's header: the block of `GEN-HEADER-IS-THE-PRODUCTS` for the styles `slash` and `block` when the type answers `headerStyle: block`, the comment of its extension (`LIC-COMMENT-STYLES`) otherwise, after the prelude; a file that cannot carry a comment receives `<name>.license` with the copyright and the SPDX line. The holder, the expression (resolved for the file's path), the year, the title and the licence file are the profile's as in `HEADER-FROM-PROFILE`. A file that already resolves to a carrier naming a policy holder and the own expression is `unchanged`; a file whose carrier names a holder outside the policy is reported as `foreign-holder` and left alone, unless `--replace-retired` is given: then the leading comment block that carries the foreign copyright line is removed and the family's header written in its place (`replaced`). `--json`: `data: {scope: "own", files: [{path, action: "header"|"sidecar"|"unchanged"|"replaced"|"foreign-holder"}]}`. Codes: 0; 1 (a file left with a foreign holder); 2 (no declaration, the store or the profile unavailable).

p.VERIFY-LICENSING: When the patch set carries `codkit.licensing.json`, `verify` adds three checks. The profile: the store on the machine must approve it, else one finding `CK-E-LICENSE-PROFILE` - the machine that verifies carries the policy, the CI machine included, and no patch-set fallback exists (`ORGANIZATION-POLICY-TRUST`). The carriers: `CONSUMER-LICENSE-CHECK` over the own layers - `delta/own/**` without the tool's delivered paths and the own manifest, and `delta/own-extensions/**` - every problem a `CK-E-LICENSE-HEADER` finding naming the file. The surfaces, for a type with the `licensing` area: every `field` is set by an overlay of its target to the value `GEN-LICENSING` would write (or, for `url` without `product.url`, removed), the add-file patch of the licence file exists and its body is the canonical text of the own expression, the component licences and the renderings are declared by add-file patches - each disagreement a `CK-E-LICENSE-SURFACE` finding naming the surface and the artifact. Without a declaration `verify` is unchanged.

p.LICENCE-GUARD: The leftover guard of the licence is one template of the engine rendered with the type's `guard(ownRoot)` words and the profile's values, written by `gen licensing` at the type's path and found by `verify` under its suite id `licence-leftovers`. In the fork tree, under the product's own test run and without the tool, it proves: every file of the own root and of every own extension - the tool's delivered directory excluded - carries a header in its first twenty non-empty lines with a copyright line naming one of the holders and exactly one `SPDX-License-Identifier` equal to the expression of its directory, or a `<name>.license` sidecar with the same two lines; no retired notice appears in any own text file or in the licence file, the renderings and the component licences; the licence file at `<licenceFileDirectory>/<licenseFile>` is byte-identical to the canonical text (its SHA-256 baked in); every `field` reads the expected value in its manifest; every component licence exists. The guard reads the tree from the directory the runner starts in and names no path of the tool; its runner words are the type's (`suite`/`test` or `describe`/`it`).
